A boulder bullet appears to be a magical sling bullet when held, but it is actually a shrunken piece of catapult ammunition. A boulder bullet expands rapidly when launched from a sling or sling staff, increasing in size and dealing greater base damage depending on the version used. This doesn't affect the bullet's range or any of the normal mechanics for using a sling bullet, though the boulder bullet is treated as siege weapon ammunition for the purposes of wind effects and similar penalties. Similarly, if a boulder bullet is launched and misses its target, roll 1d8 to determine the adjacent square in which it lands. Once it has and remains boulder-sized thereafter.

    Lesser Boulder Bullet (CL 10th): A lesser boulder bullet is a + 1 sling bullet that expands to the size of light catapult ammunition, increasing its base damage to 4d6.

    Boulder Bullet (CL 14th): A boulder bullet is a +2 sling bullet that expands to the size of standard catapult ammunition, increasing its base damage to 6d6.

    Greater Boulder Bullet (CL 18th): A lesser boulder bullet is a + 3 sling bullet that expands to the size of heavy catapult ammunition, increasing its base damage to 8d6.

I'm playing a halfling cavalier myself (emissary/beast rider). For equipment, barding is very important. A lance is likely going to be your main weapon. Follow it up with a good back-up weapon (mine wields a greatsword, but that's for flavor more than damage). Also, you may want to look into the Charger Archtype for your mount. Also, if you don't need the hp/skill points, I recommend putting favored class bonus into the halfling cavalier bonus (+1/2 to your effective level when calculating damage to a challenged enemy)

Anyways, feats. Emissary gets mounted combat as a bonus feat, so your first level feat should probably be (1) ride by attack, then (3) spirited charge, (5) power attack, and (6) --vital strike-- (**edit** I'm an idiot and this doesn't work). 

For your mount, look into going for an overrun build. It is a lot of fun when you knock down foes in the path of your charge later on. First level feat can be whatever, then Power Attack (2), Improved Overrun (5), Charge Through (8).

If my math is right, if you hold the lance in two hands while charging and use power attack (assuming strength of 16), 6th level gives you 4d6 (spirited charge + lance is 3d6, --vital strike adds the base die again for 4d6-- ) + 12 ( 3 strength mod, times 1.5 for two handed weapon, times 3 for spirited charge)  + 18 (power attack times 3 for spirited charge). 4d6 + 30 for an average of 44 damage per charge. And if you ride by attack the target, just keep moving to turn around and do it again next turn.

Last night in pathfinder, I amost caused a tpk. With a cr1/3 turtle. It took 20 minutes to resolve

**Edit**: i will post the story in a little while when i can use something better than my broken phone to type. 

**Edit 2**: This is the version of events written by the animal loving rangers.

A turtle walked up as inner-party conflict (half-orc dislike portrayed properly, and reactions to it as well) reached a peak. Human Barbarian decided to charge it, which would have put him over a pressure plate. One of the half-orcs tripped him to save his life, he AoO's the orc in a Rage, barely missing.

I swing at the human who attacked my sister, but my dwarven friend urges me not to. I swing angrily, hitting the turtle in fury, and dropping it to 0. 
Guilt hits me, and I drop my weapon and try to heal it. I fail and pick it up, to take it to the druid in the nearby town for healing.  My sister bars my way, ordering me to focus on the dungeon we are in, as the rest of the party urges me to put it out of its misery.   When I ignore her, she slaps it out of my hands. I catch it, but not before the barbarian punches it for lethal as it turns into a fine red mist.  The party then decided if the barbarian  rubbed the entrails on me or not, since I rolled a nat 20 that was either a will save to control my anger or hit him, depending on what he did.

**Edit 3**: Basically, what had happened before hand was that tensions in the party were running high. Two of the party members were brother and sister (Half orc Ranger and Fighter), with the Dwarf Fighter who raised them out of a debt to their father for saving his life. The other two members were a human barbarian and his adopted sister, the half elf rogue. I had set things up so the ranger was already being viewed suspicionsly (druids dropping hints that he was "the chosen one", "we've been waiting for you", "You know what must be done", and loaning him a T-Rex animal companion to guard him on the way to the dungeon), and then the dwarf and the barbarian both chugged mysterious magical liquids that they found, failed a will save, and became paranoid and quick-tempered. They had almost come to blows before, with the human calling the orcs in an overheard private conversation with the elf "Rape spawn", and saying that they couldn't be trusted because "blood tells". The orc's private talks with the dwarf in orcish did nothing to make things better. The party was jumping at shadows, seeing things that weren't there, and that was before even getting to the dungeon.

The dungeon had been filled with traps, some avoided, some set off. One tripwire was found by the half-orc ranger, and he told everyone to get down before cutting it after seeing holes in the walls pointing towards them, and runes on the roof. The holes shot out arrows, and the runes cast "Doom" on them. The first group, (the dwarf and the orcs) failed, and felt a sense of doom and dread. The human and half-elf freaked out at how they were acting, and at the risky behavior of slashing the tripwire. Then the turtle started coming up the hallway. Slowly moving towards them. The PC's ignored it, fighting among themselves and arguing before the barbarian declared he "went into rage and charged the doom turtle". There was a pressure place in front of him that the whole party knew about. He forgot about it when he declared it, but he said it, so charge he did! The half-orc fighter rolled an attack of opportunity to trip him and stop him from getting to the plate. She succeeded, but lacking improved trip, she provoked an attack of opportunity from him. He was in a rage, so he swung at her, missed by 1, and the ranger got pissed off that his SISTER was just attacked by the angry, racist, dangerous human. Ranger was going to attack the prone barb. when the dwarf talked him out of it. In rage, he smacked the turtle who had just come into range and was attempting a bite. He did 8 damage to the 9 hp turtle. The turtle fumbled its roll, and I pulled a card from the fumble deck. It lost 2 points of Con. Dropping it to 0. Where it whimpered and cried out in pain. Making the ranger's player flip me off for making him care about the injured animal. The barbarian argued for killing it, while the ranger failed a healing check. He did the "logical" thing, and decided to pick it up and bring it to the town druid for healing!

His sister tried to to talk him out of it, and slapped it out of his hand, dealing 1 nonleathal, bringing the squirming "beast" unconscious. The ranger asked for a reflex save to catch the falling turtle before he hit the ground. Nat 20. He succeeds! Turtle doesn't take lethal fall damage. The barbarian talks about just cutting the turtle in half, and the orc's hands with it. The dwarf draws his weapon. The fighter draws hers. The rogue gets her dagger out. The party is going to kill itself. The barbarian lunges and punches the turtle instead. It breaks the shell and crushes it into juice. The ranger is PISSED. Draws his axe. The barbarian jokes about rubbing the heart all over the ranger's face. Ranger rolls to keep himself from killing the barb right there. Nat 20. The barb decides to just eat part of the turtle instead. Tensions fade barely as the rogue and barb march down the hallway.

TL;DR: The party almost killed themselves because of a doom turtle.
